en.sup: Supplied in English. The Greek has only the article and the father's name in the genitive, 'the (one) of Alphaeus'.

01.r: Links this scene to the one before.

02.r: Jesus is on his way past the place.
02.n: Abbott-Smith lists this verse under the intransitive sense 'to pass by'. A present participle: it happens as he goes. The Geneva names Jesus as the subject; the Greek leaves it to the verb.

03.r: Jesus sees Levi at his post.

04.r: The man called, named here by his father.
04.n: Abbott-Smith lists this verse under Levi son of Alphaeus, with a cross-reference to his entry for Matthew, and notes that a marginal reading of Westcott and Hort has a form of the name James here. That Levi and the Matthew of Matthew 9:9 are one man is the usual reading of the two call scenes; it is an inference, not stated in this verse.

05.r: The article stands for 'son', which the Greek leaves understood.

06.r: The article before the father's name; English does not use it.

07.n: Abbott-Smith gives the Aramaic form חַלְפַּי and lists this verse under 'Father of Levi', keeping him apart from the Alphaeus who is the father of James.

10.r: A particular booth, the one at that place.

11.r: The post where tolls were collected.
11.n: Abbott-Smith defines it as 'a custom house, tollhouse, place of toll', and derives it from τελώνης, toll collector; this study renders it 'toll booth' to keep it with that family. The translations range from the KJV's 'receipt of custom' to the BSB's 'tax booth'.

12.r: Joins what Jesus says to what he sees.

13.n: The present tense in a past narrative, which makes the moment vivid. This study keeps the present, 'says'.

15.r: A call to come with Jesus as his disciple.
15.n: Abbott-Smith gives 'to accompany, follow' and a figurative sense 'of discipleship'. A present imperative, which the YLT brings out with 'Be following': an ongoing following, not one step.

16.r: Jesus himself, the one to be followed.

18.r: He stands up from his seat at the booth.
18.n: An aorist participle, literally 'having risen', joined to 'followed'. Abbott-Smith treats the second aorist, the form here, as intransitive.

19.r: He leaves the booth and goes with Jesus.
